subject.title: feat(sandbox): add sbx as a sandbox backend alongside OpenShell

question: Should Docker Sandboxes be accepted as an officially catalogued OpenClaw sandbox backend, rather than remaining an independently distributed plugin or ClawHub package?
rationale: The patch is technically shaped as an externalized plugin, but it adds an official package/catalog entry, public configuration, docs, and dependency ownership that require a maintainer decision beyond mechanical review.

options.title: Sponsor the official plugin
options.body: Accept `sbx` as an official external plugin after real-runtime proof and exact-head dependency authorization are supplied.

options.title: Route to independent distribution
options.body: Keep the implementation outside the official catalog and publish it as an independently maintained ClawHub or npm plugin using the existing sandbox SDK seam.

options.title: Defer backend support
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers define the supported Docker Sandboxes lifecycle, isolation, and release-ownership expectations.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the official plugin
recommendation.body: Accept `sbx` as an official external plugin after real-runtime proof and exact-head dependency authorization are supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only directly evidenced person connected to the current implementation, though final product ownership should be assigned by repository maintainers.
